execution.milestone_plans: This sprint runs on the current loop, so Phase B applies. Every item builds at once, so dispatch the M1 (066-03..07), M2 (066-08..10) and M3 (066-11, 066-12) Architect plans in parallel at kickoff, after C0. Each item's first dispatch waits only for its own milestone's plan. Milestones are groupings, not build separators. M2 and M3 plans are written against C1, C2 and the pinned_interfaces below.
execution.merge_lane: One item at a time. DevOps merges story/<ID> into cli main with --no-ff (local only, no push, no publish), then runs the full npm test, plus the integration suites for the known-red check (see dist_rule for where). Teardown after merge, with both git status --porcelain empty: remove the cli worktree first, then the outer host.
execution.merge_order_rule: The merge lane takes items as they pass QA-Verify, subject to upstream (stories.<ID>.upstream is authoritative; waves[] is a view). Among layer-0 items, when two are ready at once the critical path goes first: 03 and 04 (they unblock 08), then 07 (unblocks 09), 05 (unblocks 10 and 09), and 06 (unblocks 11). 08, 09 and 10 are fail-safe-serialized: they merge one at a time, never together. They share no edge, so a ready one merges ahead of one that is not ready; on a tie the order is 08, 09, 10. 11 merges after all five of its upstreams; 12 merges last. Swapping the merge order of two items with no upstream between them makes the later one re-integrate main and re-run QA-Verify (flashcard 2026-11-10 #merge #contract); preview with git merge-tree.

execution.tests: Build lanes run npm run typecheck and targeted test files only (npm run test:file -- <file>). The full npm test runs only in the merge lane. execution.integration: An item integrates only after every upstream item has merged into cli main. In its cli worktree: git merge --no-ff main. On a conflict in a shared file the owner's region wins and the item re-applies its own insertions. A conflict inside an existing or red test goes to QA-Red, never the Developer. Never hand-merge a generated file: run npm run gen:codex and confirm prebuild's build-codex-payload.mjs --check passes (npm run gen:codex -- --check ignores --check; flashcard 2026-11-10 #codegen #gen-codex). Then re-run prebuild, typecheck and the item's targeted tests, and run QA-Verify on the integrated tree. If main moves before the merge, integrate again.

frozen_exports: cleargate-cli/scaffold/core/.cleargate/scripts/segment_stages.mjs: export const STAGE_NAMES: readonly string[] = Object.freeze(['story-plan', 'qa-red', 'architect-tpv', 'developer', 'qa-verify', 'architect-review', 'merge']), in this order.

cleargate-cli/scaffold/core/.cleargate/scripts/segment_stages.mjs: export function stagesFor(lane: unknown): ReadonlyArray<Readonly<Stage>>. Synchronous; returns a fresh frozen array of frozen objects on every call. Stage = { name: string, kind: 'agent' | 'barrier-script', agent?: 'architect' | 'qa' | 'developer', mode?: string, when: 'always' | 'scan-flagged', script?: string }.

Stage definitions: story-plan = agent architect, mode STORY-PLAN; qa-red = agent qa, mode RED; architect-tpv = agent architect, mode TPV; developer = agent developer, no mode; qa-verify = agent qa, mode VERIFY; architect-review = agent architect, mode POST-FLIGHT; merge = kind barrier-script, script 'merge_story.mjs'. All other stages are kind agent.

Lane lists: fast = developer, merge. standard = qa-red, architect-tpv (scan-flagged), developer, qa-verify, architect-review (scan-flagged), merge. runtime = story-plan, qa-red, architect-tpv (scan-flagged), developer, qa-verify, architect-review (always), merge. Any stage not marked scan-flagged is when 'always'. An unknown, missing or non-string lane, or a name that is not an own key (e.g. 'constructor'), returns the standard list.

cleargate-cli/scaffold/core/.cleargate/scripts/segment_stages.mjs: export function laneOf(storyId: string, ctx: { state?: object | null, plan?: object | null }): string. Returns state.stories[storyId].lane when it is a string, else plan.lane_assignments[storyId], else 'standard'. It does not validate the name.

Interface implemented by STORY-066-06, not by the skeleton: the segment verdict gains lane: string and stages_run: string[]. validateVerdicts(verdicts, { mode: 'wave' | 'serial' }) requires both in both modes. Every stages_run entry must be a stage name of the verdict's normalised lane, and names may repeat. A GREEN verdict's stages_run contains every kind 'agent', when 'always' stage of its lane. qaSha may be null on a GREEN verdict only when the lane's stages include no qa agent stage. Errors keep the form 'Malformed segment verdict for <storyId>: <reason>.'

Interface implemented by STORY-066-06: launchWave({ ..., lanes }), with segments carrying lane and stages, and segmentRunner(story, runId, { lane, stages }); dispatchSerial({ ..., lanes }); the dispatch line of node dispatch_serial.mjs next gains lane and stages.

open_decisions_for_gate_2: 1. Confirm nested cli worktrees for SPRINT-46 (ruling (a) layout). This clears the BUG-046 refusal for this sprint only. Correct the Risks row that says 'branches in the cli main checkout'.
2. Confirm C1 as a data-complete skeleton (the stage table is the contract) and C2 as a stub (extractFailing returns []), frozen as written.

3. Scan lane routing vs merge_story.mjs: run from the main checkout, pre_gate_runner.sh resolves STORY_ID from story/<ID> and state from .active, then applies STORY-022-04 routing. For a fast item, a failing scan is demoted by the scan and again by merge_story R4, appends an LD line to the authored sprint markdown (which R5 then refuses as authored dirt, exit 2, on every later merge), and gets demoted even when the baseline excuses the failure; a passing scan writes 'Architect Passed'. Recommended: CR:spec-clarification so that 066-03 adds CLEARGATE_SCAN_NO_LANE_ROUTING=1 (skip the routing block) and 066-08 sets it, making merge_story.mjs the only writer of demotion and state.

4. 066-08 R5 stashes derived files in the main checkout. Flashcard 2026-09-26 #worktree #git #danger: the stash stack is shared by every worktree; never stash. Recommended: CR:spec-clarification to copy the allowlisted paths aside and restore them after the merge, with the same rule that the merged side wins for wiki paths. Alternative: keep stash but pop by the exact ref recorded at push, after checking its message.

5. Add scripts/clean-room/loop-script.mjs to 066-06's section 3.1 (its verdict literal at :214 must gain lane and stages_run, or codex-loop-harness.red fails in npm test and the clean-room release gate breaks).

6. Doc drift no story owns: reporter.md:39-40 (+ reporter.toml) still quotes GOAL_RELATION from each milestone plan, which 066-12 removes, so SPRINT-47's Reporter would find none. cleargate-protocol.md:28 and :951, core/.cleargate/README.md:48 and hosts/claude/CLAUDE.md:20 still say DevOps merges. templates/story.md:137 points at the milestone plan. Recommended: widen 066-12's section 3.1 by CR:spec-clarification. Alternative: intake for SPRINT-47 (reporter.md at least should not wait).

7. 066-12 build timing. (A, recommended) build from C1 at kickoff against P1-P7, and confirm against merged code at integration. (B) as written: start its build after 066-11 merges, which adds a full build cycle to the tail.
8. Merge-lane known reds (canonical-live-parity 5a, 5b, 5c; qa-content slice parity; doctor drift): record each in section 6 and do not hand-port live.
9. No BD on cli main during the sprint; run post-merge full suites in a throwaway worktree at main's tip.

10. Earlier-sprint sealed red tests edited by 066-06 (six .red files), 066-10 (sprint-metrics.red) and 066-12 (codex-sprint-execution-render.red) are written in each item's QA-Red commit, never the Developer's. The cli repo has no commit hooks, so this rule is by role only.
